input.quote: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position, not merely the fallback. Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for it and contains an express present assignment by Vendor of all worldwide right, title, and interest (plus equivalent assignments from Vendor personnel). Section 14.3 confines Vendor's retained rights to "Vendor Technology," defined in Section 1.8 as Vendor's pre-existing technology and expressly excluding Customer Data and IP Customer owned before the Effective Date, and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the Section 13.2 licence back, which is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" to use, modify, create derivative works from and permit contractors to support for Customer's business — covering the perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free elements. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and Customer-provided material, and the only right passing to Vendor is the limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer, which is service delivery rather than independent exploitation; Section 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training absent our express written consent (a consent gate, not a standing licence). Section 14.4 creates no jointly owned IP unless both Parties sign a separate instrument identifying exploitation rights, which we control. No provision assigns Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor, so there is no walk-away exposure. Two adjacent points are noted only, not redlined here: Section 13.1's revocable, non-transferable Services licence excluding Affiliates and contractors is a Services-access problem for the LICENSE rule (and is partly answered by Section 13.3), and Section 11.1's immediate deletion language is a TRANSITION issue; neither dilutes the ownership and Customer Data direction this rule tests, and we do not flag the same term twice.
